clue.text: Light drink the foreign politician provided

parts.note: spirit is strong alcoholic drink such as whisky or gin
la is 'the' in French, a foreign language
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician is plied with a drink by someone from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like an adjective for the drink, but it is the definition, a noun. 'provided' just links the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp burning methylated spirit is a small source of illumination, so it is a kind of light.

clue.text: Snake crushes head of this bird in part of Africa

indicators.note: a boa squeezes its prey, so here the snake's letters wrap tightly round the others

parts.note: a boa is a large constricting snake

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a swan is a large water bird

explanation.surface: A constrictor squeezes the head of a bird somewhere in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Botswana is a country in southern Africa, so it is a region of that continent.

clue.text: Theologian's guess

definitions.meaning: a theologian is a churchman learned in religion, and the possessive 's here stands for 'is'
to guess is to work something out by intuition or conjecture

explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Theologian's' reads as 'is', joining the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A divine is a clergyman expert in theology, and to divine is to conjecture by insight.

clue.text: Austrian composer about to enter Britain, all upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the whole assembled word upside down, so it reads from bottom to top
to enter means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: GB is the abbreviation for Great Britain
re is Latin for 'concerning', a common short form of about

explanation.surface: A composer from Austria comes to Britain and everyone is unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'all upset' turns the whole assembly bottom to top; 'to enter' sets one short piece inside the other first.
explanation.definitionFit: Alban Berg was a Viennese composer of the Second Viennese School, known for the opera Wozzeck.

clue.text: Paper redrafted by Tory is neat

indicators.note: a redrafted text has been rewritten, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A document rewritten by a Conservative is said to be tidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redrafted' rearranges TORY IS NEAT; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Stationery is writing materials, chiefly sheets of writing paper and envelopes.

clue.text: Small measure appropriate in the Queen Vic?

definitions.meaning: a tiny length on a ruler, one twenty-fourth of a foot
the Queen Vic is the pub in the London soap EastEnders, where cockney rhyming slang is spoken; there this phrase rhymes with pinch, meaning to steal or appropriate

explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang replaces a word with a rhyming phrase: here a phrase rhyming with 'pinch' means steal. The Queen Vic is the pub in the London TV soap EastEnders.
explanation.definitionFit: Half of an inch is a tiny unit of length, and in rhyming slang it means to steal.

clue.text: Ice creams served up in most of Italy, for example

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the letters are written from bottom to top
most of a word drops its final letter

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, Latin for for example

explanation.surface: Ice creams are dished out across most of Italy, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns the whole joined string, read bottom to top in this down clue; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelato is Italian for ice cream, and the plural is used for several frozen desserts.

clue.text: What Gladys is, at heart

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, so drop the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Asking what Gladys is really like, deep down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at heart' takes the middle of GLADYS, dropping its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladys is a woman's name, so its bearer is a woman or female person.

clue.text: Showing foresight, supply collection of books

parts.note: to supply something is to provide it
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Being forward-looking, someone stocks a library.
explanation.definitionFit: Provident means planning wisely for the future, as with savings put aside.

clue.text: Scene of conflict near troubled Asian capital

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters of the word before it are shaken up
the capital of a word is its first, capital letter

explanation.surface: Fighting is close to an Asian capital in turmoil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges NEAR to AREN; 'capital' of Asian gives A. 'Asian capital' looks like a city, but it means only the initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a place where combat or contest happens, as gladiators fought in Roman ones.

clue.text: Appearing relaxed about fraud

parts.note: re is Latin for 'concerning', a common short form of about
a sting is a confidence trick or swindle

explanation.surface: Someone looks calm while concerned with a swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: A resting face or pose looks at ease, idle or reposed.

clue.text: Quarrel with no particular girl

parts.note: a tiff is a petty quarrel
any means no particular one, as in 'any old thing'

explanation.surface: Falling out with no girl in particular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiffany is a girl's first name.

clue.text: Discover a very small amount

definitions.meaning: to discover is to track down or find, as by following clues
a tiny quantity, a hint or vestige of something

explanation.definitionFit: To trace a person is to find them; a trace of poison is a minute quantity.

clue.text: Clumsily loads iron studs

indicators.note: done clumsily means done awkwardly, so these letters are jumbled up

explanation.surface: Someone awkwardly heaps up iron fixings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clumsily' rearranges LOADS IRON; 'studs' is the definition, not the iron.
explanation.definitionFit: Large-headed nails were hammered into old doors as decorative studs.

clue.text: Think shop worker can catch rodent

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a food shop

indicators.note: the worker is able to catch, so it holds the rodent inside

parts.note: the worker bee is the crossword's standard worker
a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: A shop assistant might be able to trap a rat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shop worker' looks like one person, but it splits into a shop and an insect; 'can catch' then holds the rodent inside the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliberate is to ponder or consider carefully before deciding.

clue.text: Dockers taking woman and daughter through warehouses

indicators.note: a piece running through the middle of another sits inside it

parts.note: stores are buildings for keeping goods
Eve is the first woman in Genesis and a common crossword woman
D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: Dock workers bring a mother and daughter through warehouses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevedores load and unload ships in port, the work of dock labourers.

clue.text: Western movie romance — all heads turn

indicators.note: to turn here means to change round, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: In a cowboy film's love story, everyone looks round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' rearranges ROMANCE ALL HEADS; 'heads turn' reads as people staring.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1970 film starring Richard Harris is a western about an Englishman captured by the Sioux.

clue.text: Singer behind bars

parts.note: a singer is a songbird, and the bars are those of its cage; the surface suggests a vocalist in prison

explanation.definitionFit: A canary or finch kept in a cage is a songster confined behind wire bars.

clue.text: Trailing wild creature

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A wild animal is following behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges TRAILING to give a mammal with a banded tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringtail is an animal with a ringed tail, such as the ringtail cat or a possum.

clue.text: Peasant who'll get bread and cheese lunch later on?

definitions.text: Peasant who'll get bread and cheese lunch later on?

parts.words: Peasant who'll get bread and cheese lunch later on?
parts.note: a ploughman's lunch is bread and cheese, so a young farm lad will one day be a ploughman entitled to it

explanation.walkthrough: A ploughman's lunch is a British pub meal of bread, cheese and pickle.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustic lad who guides the team at the plough is a young farm worker.

clue.text: Patient man going after unusual casual work

indicators.note: going after means placed behind, so the patient man comes second

parts.note: odd means unusual
Job is the biblical figure famed for his patience

explanation.surface: A patient fellow follows something strange to find some piecework.
explanation.definitionFit: Odd jobs are occasional small tasks done for pay, irregular work.

clue.text: Coins enclosed in empty package

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation is placed inside the emptied word
an emptied word keeps only its first and last letters

parts.note: enc. is the standard abbreviation for enclosed, written on letters with enclosures

explanation.surface: Money is sealed inside a hollow parcel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' reduces PACKAGE to PE, and 'in' puts ENC inside it. 'enclosed' looks like part of the surface but gives its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Pence are small British coins, a hundred to the pound.

clue.text: Refrain from taking old man's drink

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, the old man, and the 's adds S
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Someone declines to take Dad's drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass up an offer is to decline it or let it go by.

clue.text: Willie Carson, for example, races topless

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: Ascot is the famous racecourse and race meeting in Berkshire

explanation.surface: The jockey Willie Carson rides at a meeting where the hats come off.
explanation.walkthrough: Willie Carson, the champion jockey, was born in Scotland. Royal Ascot is a famous English horse-race meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Carson was born in Stirling, so he is a native of Scotland, an example of a person from there.

clue.text: After start of repast, one's presented with German dish

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: one is I, and 's adds S
Otto is a typical German man's name

explanation.surface: After the opening of a meal, an Italian rice plate is served by a German.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' and 'presented with' just place and join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian rice dish cooked slowly in stock.

clue.text: Leader of regiment needing help in attack

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: The head of a regiment needs reinforcements during an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A raid is a sudden assault on an enemy position.

clue.text: Smell from river reported

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the word sounds like the one entered

parts.note: the Oder is a river in central Europe on the German-Polish border

explanation.surface: A bad whiff comes from the river, people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An odour is a scent or whiff, often unpleasant.

clue.text: Left winger, one accepted by ethnic group

indicators.note: accepted by means taken in, so the one goes inside the group

parts.note: a tribe is a social or ethnic group
a unit is a single thing, one

explanation.surface: A left-wing player is welcomed into a community.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tribunite supports the Tribune group of left-wing Labour MPs; 'winger' suggests a footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribunites were Labour MPs on the party's left, linked to the Tribune newspaper.
